This is the one-day workshop on the EU-frames case. It works on a study of Eurobarometer surveys, which asked whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the member states frame the European Union, and on a claim of the original author (OA) that five analysts reanalysed in the Multi100 project. Across the day you work as analyst no. 6. In the morning you meet the arguments and the evidence on the credibility of social science and the three kinds of repetition that go under the word 'replication', read the paper with what SCORE found when it tried to reproduce and to replicate it, write the estimand behind the claim and finish a causal graph for it. In the afternoon you reproduce, to the third decimal, the result that Multi100 recorded for one of the three analysts whose analyses rest on means of countries or of cells, whichever you choose, and the three reproduced models lead into the problem of few clusters. Then the specification menu is taken apart decision by decision: you explore it and put an exploratory dot on the live class chart, read the chart against the curve of 864 specifications of the claim, and declare one analysis in a shortened preregistration before you run it and submit it as a declared dot.

You leave with an estimand and a causal graph of your own, a reproduced result, two dots on the class chart, one explored and one declared, and the place of your result on the curve of 864.

## How you work

The day is taught mainly in the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with nothing to install. It works on aggregate data only, the country-year panel of the course and two files that the course rebuilt for two of the analysts, and the lab holds all three; the respondents themselves are a subject of the third day of the Extended course. Open the lab in a tab of its own and keep this page open beside it. Each part of the day has a page that lists its steps in order, and every step that you work at the keyboard has a button that opens the lab at the right task, or the page on which the work is done. The workspace that you install before the day, in your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), holds the same tasks and gives the same numbers. The slides are on the [slides page](slides.qmd), and each part opens with a link to its place in the deck.

[Open the browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

Several of the steps are things that the class does together, such as everyone typing the value that they have just reproduced and holding it back until the facilitator says go, so the day needs a facilitator. Some stretches of the slides are optional, the tutorial on the methods behind the menu and the background of the multiverse in the last part, and the facilitator switches them on or off to suit the class. The day runs in four parts, with a break after the first and the third and lunch after the second.

## The parts of the day

- **[Before the day](before.qmd).** You install R and the workspace, work through the first module on R, and read the case study.
- **[Part 1 – The claim and credibility](part-1.qmd).** The part sets out the credibility debate, what 'replication' names, Multi100 from the inside and the paper with its record in SCORE, and it ends with R running on your machine.
- **[Part 2 – The estimand and the causal graph](part-2.qmd).** You meet estimands and a short course on causal graphs, and then you write the estimand and finish the graph.
- **[Part 3 – The reproduction](part-3.qmd).** You reproduce the result of C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL, read the three models side by side, meet the problem of few clusters, and read the code that your analyst deposited.
- **[Part 4 – Robustness](part-4.qmd).** You work the menu and put an exploratory dot on the class chart, read the chart against the curve of 864, ask what the curve establishes and what a replication would have to fix, and declare one analysis before it runs.
- **[After the day](after.qmd).** The page says where to go next in the companion curriculum.

[Start with Before the day](before.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

The same case is also taught as the [Extended course](../eu-frames-extended/index.qmd), whose second day is this workshop, and as a [self-study route](../self-study/index.qmd).
